key_insight: A simulation-trained deep learning platform can automate interpretation of CDC and FCXM HLA antibody assays while handling the variability of real-world pre-transplant lab imaging.
clinical_relevance: Automated, traceable crossmatch readouts may reduce operator dependence and improve consistency in pre-transplant compatibility assessment.
method: Generated CDC-like simulated training images covering variability in resolution, staining, cell density, clustering, and background fluorescence.
Used a UNet-based workflow for lymphocyte segmentation, experiment-specific fluorescence classification, and well-level cytotoxicity scoring.
Added automated FCXM interpretation with cell-population identification and IgG readouts in a web-based platform with API access.
evidence_signal: In abstract-level evaluation, the simulation-trained model outperformed a conventional rule-based pipeline under variable acquisition conditions and matched performance to the range of human inter-annotator variability.
watch_item: Performance depends on assay-specific image quality and careful validation before routine deployment across different laboratories and instruments.
paper_title: Simulation-Trained Deep Learning for Automated Cell-Based HLA Antibody Assay Interpretation in Pre-Transplant Diagnostics
